title: adaptive-histogram-bucketer: delta-smoothing + kernel-fit scoring
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: long tail variability in sequence length causes padding waste or high latency when using fixed buckets. This PR introduces an Adaptive Histogram Bucketer (AHB) that builds a lightweight, time-decayed histogram of request sequence lengths and performs delta-smoothing to avoid oscillatory re-bucketing. We combine that with a kernel-fit scoring function that selects bucket cut points to minimize expected padded token cost while honoring latency SLOs.

What this change does:
- New bucketer module (serve/batching/ahb.rs) that maintains a sliding-window histogram keyed by rounded seqlen and a decay factor.
- Delta-smoothing: when histogram shifts, changes to bucket boundaries are applied gradually over a configurable cooldown window to avoid destabilizing continuous batching.
- Kernel-fit scoring: we score candidate bucketizations by simulating kernel efficiency (per-bucket kernel cost model from serve/scheduler/kernel_cost_model.rs) and expected padding overhead; objective minimizes token-cost + kernel-penalty subject to p95 latency budget.
- Lazy KV prefill heuristics: when a request is added to a bucket and the bucket is predicted to be kernel-optimal, we trigger a lightweight KV prefill probe (serve/kv/prefill.rs) to warm common crypto keys and KV cache entries for likely continuation tokens; probe is rate-limited per-bucket.
- Continuous batching integration: bucketer exports a suggested packing plan to the existing continuous batch composer (serve/batching/composer.rs) with a soft-eviction policy to avoid long waits.
- Tests & benchmarks: end-to-end integration test, unit tests for smoothing and kernel-fit, and a micro-benchmark harness (bench/ahb_bench.rs).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The histogram is intentionally low-memory (bucketed to powers-of-two and capped counts) to keep overhead sub-millisecond per request. Delta-smoothing prevents churn in the composer that previously increased latency variance.
- Kernel-fit scoring relies on an empirical kernel cost surface (linearized model loaded from serve/scheduler/kernel_cost_model.rs) so it remains fast; we allow a conservative fallback to size-based bucketing if model confidence is low.
- KV prefill is conservative: it does not prefetch model weights or large KV entries, only small warm entries and KV indices used by common tokenization continuation heuristics. This reduces thundering-herd risk on cold buckets.

Outcomes (internal canary):
- Median per-request padded tokens reduced by ~18% for mixed chat workloads (median seqlen 32, 10% tail >256).
- P95 latency improved by ~7% under 75% utilization on an 8xA100 serving pod.
- Overall token throughput improved by ~9% for throughput-oriented clusters due to fewer padded tokens and better kernel packing.

Why this is different from previous bucketers: unlike fixed quantile or simple seqlen bucketers, AHB reacts to distribution shifts with smoothing and explicitly reasons about kernel execution characteristics when deciding cut points. This reduces waste while keeping composer stability.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on correctness of decay math (ahb.rs), safety of delta-smoothing transitions (composer glue), and potential KV prefill contention (prefill.rs). The kernel cost adapter is deliberately conservative; consider whether we should expose a more sophisticated model in a follow-up.
